items.question: Fill the gap: 'Yesterday I ___ rice for dinner.'
items.explanation: 'Eat' is an irregular verb, so its past form is 'ate', not 'eated'. We use 'eaten' after have or has: 'I have eaten'.

items.question: In the sentence 'She runs quickly', the word 'quickly' is an adverb.
items.explanation: An adverb tells us how, when or where an action happens. 'Quickly' tells us how she runs. Many adverbs end in -ly, like slowly, softly and happily.
items.source: Wren & Martin, High School English Grammar and Composition

items.question: Fill the gap: 'This is the ___ day of my life.'
items.explanation: 'Good' is irregular: good, better, best. Use 'best' when comparing one thing with all others. 'Goodest' is not a real English word.

items.question: Fill in the missing word: 'Neither Ravi ___ Sita came to the party.'
items.explanation: 'Neither' goes with 'nor', and 'either' goes with 'or'. The sentence means Ravi did not come, and Sita did not come either.
items.source: Wren & Martin, High School English Grammar and Composition

items.question: Which sentence is the passive voice of 'The cat chased the mouse'?
options: The cat was chased by the mouse.
The mouse was chased by the cat.
The mouse is chased by the cat.
items.explanation: In the passive voice, the object (the mouse) comes first, then 'was/were' + past form, then 'by' + the doer. The action is in the past, so we use 'was chased', not 'is chased'.
items.source: Wren & Martin, High School English Grammar and Composition
